newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber end firm ahead of holiday weekend.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber end firm ahead of holiday weekend.

text.p: Rubber futures closed steady to firmer on Friday in line with firmer Japanese prices and mild shortcovering ahead of the long holiday weekend, dealers said.

"There was some kind of shortcovering by some consumers. The market was also helped by the higher prices in Japan," a local rubber trader said. The market will be closed on Monday, November 11, for a holiday and will reopen on Tuesday, November 12.
Tokyo's benchmark April contract gained 0.3 yen to settle at 143.2 while Kobe's April contract settled at 142.9 against the previous day's settlement of 142.0 yen.
"The shortcovering was mainly triggered by European consumers buying ahead of the holidays. The market was basically steady," a dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, December RSS3 was seen at 126.00-127.00 U.S. cents a kg compared with the previous 126.50 cents.
January RSS1 was seen at 183.00-185.00 Singapore cents (US$1.30-$1.32) a kg against 184.00 cents.
January TSR20 was seen at 178.00-180.00 Singapore cents (US$1.27-$1.28) a kg from 178.75 cents.
